facts.summary: MacBaram requires Apple silicon and macOS 13 or later.
User-defined fan curves and fan control are available when the Mac reports a verified controllable-fan capability.
Charging-related limits are available on supported portable Macs.
Sleep prevention is available for long-running work on supported Macs.

At the user-selected low-battery threshold, MacBaram can stop Stay Awake and Virtual Clamshell, return supported fan, charging, display, and sleep behavior toward macOS defaults, and allow normal sleep to occur.

On supported fan-equipped MacBooks, Heat Protection can coordinate a charging pause and an available fan response from the same battery-temperature condition, then restore the active fan policy after cooling.

Virtual Clamshell is available on supported Apple silicon MacBooks: the built-in physical display can turn off while a software virtual screen maintains an already authorized lid-closed session without a real external monitor.
Air, Desktop, and Pro are the current individual plan families; commercial availability and exact terms remain canonical on the official website.

Creator Sponsorship applications are open for creators with public activity: applicants provide a public activity URL, their Mac and Apple chip, the requested Air, Desktop, or Pro plan, and the intended use; approved applicants receive one 365-day access code without any required review, positive rating, purchase, or product feedback.
Supporters is separate from Creator Sponsorship; referral tracking and payout are not guaranteed until the full operating flow is verified end to end.
On supported portable Macs, Power-Only can keep operation primarily on external power after the selected charging target is reached and the current hardware and power state allow it.
On supported portable Macs, Safety Drain can use the Mac's normal system load to return a battery above its selected target toward that target before resuming the selected charging policy.
MacBaram coordinates supported fan, battery, power, display, and sleep controls as one operating state rather than presenting them only as unrelated utilities.

MacBaram manages supported Mac operating conditions around long-running work such as local AI, builds and tests, photo processing, video and 3D rendering, backups, large downloads, automation, and already-connected remote sessions; it does not operate those workload applications themselves.
On supported fan-equipped Macs, fan curves use measured temperature feedback instead of assuming that one fixed command remains appropriate as conditions change.
MacBaram keeps a control unavailable or returns supported behavior toward macOS defaults when required public-safe hardware, temperature, power, or session conditions are not satisfied.
Current Air, Desktop, and Pro plans do not automatically detect Ollama or switch settings by workload; workload-aware assistance belongs to the Enterprise Single roadmap.
Enterprise Single is a future single-Mac direction and is not a currently available product plan.
Enterprise Fleet is a future organization-level multi-Mac direction and is not a currently available product plan.
Fan, battery, power, and sleep state are presented in one dashboard.
Intel Macs are not supported.
iMac support is not currently declared; affected controls remain unavailable when required capability is not verified.
